candidates.description: Reuse the reference zero-ROM method unchanged on release v1 (train 445 incl. 120 hflip rows, development_test 85) to obtain this run's own measured reference after the iteration-1 backbone outage. CPU-only, no checkpoint, no code change; defect side uses the calibrated physical measurement rule.
candidates.expected_gain: Reference point (delta 0 by construction). Expected measured PLCC in the 0.66-0.85 band driven by gate accuracy (docs: single regressor ~0.66, oracle gate ~0.85). No claim of meeting the 0.85 PLCC/SRCC floors; defect macro-F1 expected well below 0.85 and capped at 0.80 by zero white_balance support.
candidates.cost_estimate: 1 experiment, CPU-only (sklearn ensembles on cached 82-d+16-d features), < 3 min wall clock, 0 GPU, 0 new samples, ROM estimate ~0.05 MB (descriptor rules + small calibration table).
failure_conditions: Unknown signature of score_moe.run/predict -> the evaluator harness cannot invoke it; report as plugin-interface failure rather than a negative result.
dev.jsonl/eval_inputs.jsonl absent under QAA_ROOT -> FileNotFoundError from config/data resolution; infrastructure failure, not evidence against the method.
Reported per-class F1 must include support; quoting an all-class macro-F1 without stating the 0-support white_balance class would be misleading.
Not a new independent acceptance test: the historical eval split is already exposed; results are replication-only.
Do not treat this reuse run as evidence that deep backbone features are unhelpful — that route was never measured (missing assets).
candidates.implementation_goal: ARCHITECTURE: no code change; run the plugin method algorithm_plugins/iqa/methods/score_moe.py, which fits three complementary views on dev only (ExtraTrees+RF global regressor; 4-class classifier decoded as E[score]=sum_k P(level=k)*level_mean; explicit gate P(defective|x) x degradation-family router x per-severity experts) on 82-d degradation features + 16-d physical measurements + optional file-size metadata, blended by subject-group CV on dev. LOSS: not gradient-trained; selection is by dev-only CV of the blend weight (blend_step). TRAINING: deterministic seed 7, 4 CV folds, 3 ensemble seeds, min_family_rows 15, <=40 iterations per estimator; eval labels never read. PREDICTION: score clipped to 0-100; defects from the zero-ROM calibrated measurement rule (measure_lib thresholds). EXPORT: record preds.jsonl (path/image, score, 5 defect flags), config.json, rom_estimate.json, per-class support and wall clock under runs/<run_id>/; no fp16 weights exist on this path, so state the export deviation explicitly.

candidates.description: Minimal modify of score_moe in model_pool/: an import shim that re-exports signature-agnostic run(*a, **k)/predict(*a, **k) wrappers around the frozen plugin module, updates only DEFAULTS keys verified to exist at import time, applies a dev-out-of-fold monotone calibration to the blended score, and exposes an augmentation dose flag (0/120/240 flipped rows) for the already-materialised hflip data.
candidates.expected_gain: Calibration: PLCC +0.00 to +0.03 (monotone map cannot change SRCC by construction). CV/blend hparams: +0.00 to +0.02 PLCC. Augmentation dose 240 vs 0: +0.00 to +0.02 supported-class macro-F1 if flare/glare statistics are not direction-sensitive; 5-class defect macro-F1 stays capped at 0.80.
candidates.cost_estimate: 1 coded method (small shim, model_pool/score_moe_calibrated_dose/method.py), ~4 CPU-only runs (dose 0/120/240 + identity-calibration control), <=40 iterations each, plus 1 extra cached feature pass for the new flipped rows; no GPU, no checkpoint, ROM ~0.05 MB.
failure_conditions: Fix budget is exhausted (max_fix_attempts 2/2 used): any syntax/import error terminates this candidate as failed. Mitigation: ast.parse plus a 5-row dry predict before the full run; wrapper must use (*a, **k) so an unknown run/predict signature cannot break it.

If 'from algorithm_plugins.iqa.methods import score_moe' fails due to relative-import/package context (score_moe uses 'from . import common, measure_lib'), report as an interface failure and fall back to c1; do not retry blindly.

If no dev out-of-fold score hook is exposed, the fallback is a 4-level monotone map fitted on training folds only; if dev PLCC changes by < +0.01 under both, report calibration as unsupported and revert to c1.
If rows in the release carry no 'augmented' tag, the 0/120/240 dose ablation is unimplementable: report the augmentation effect as UNMEASURABLE, not as neutral.
Isotonic on ~445 rows with many ties (severity-quantised pseudo-MOS) can overfit; check split-half dev stability before export.
Counter-signal: hflip changes flare/glare blob geometry; if flare per-class F1 falls versus dose 0, augmentation is not label-preserving for that class.
Any claim that defect_macro_f1/hardcase_macro_f1 gates are met would require label or coverage change: prohibited. white_balance support is 0 and the annotation budget (4/4) is spent.
If only the base module's DEFAULTS exists and no calibration hook is reachable, the calibration term is inert; report it as not implemented rather than claiming a calibration gain.
ablations: A0 = c1 reference (unchanged score_moe, same split/seed).
A1 = c2 code, augmentation dose 0 -> isolates the calibration + hyperparameter change.
A2 = c2 code, dose 120; A3 = c2 code, dose 240 -> dose-response for the data intervention (requires augmented-row tagging).
A4 = identity calibration vs isotonic-on-dev-OOF -> isolates calibration.
A5 = plugin-default defect thresholds vs dev-OOF tuned thresholds -> isolates threshold tuning.
Score-head-only control if reachable: disable the family/severity experts and keep the global regressor -> attributes any gain to the MoE routing.
candidates.implementation_goal: ARCHITECTURE: new file model_pool/score_moe_calibrated_dose/method.py that imports the frozen plugin module and re-exports run(*a, **k)/predict(*a, **k). At import it updates only keys present in score_moe.DEFAULTS against a whitelist (missing keys are dropped and logged, never invented); wraps predict's score output with a monotone calibration map loaded from calibration.json (isotonic breakpoints fitted on dev out-of-fold predictions; fallback = 4-level monotone map using level means fitted on training folds only) and clips to [0,100]; passes the 5 defect flags through unchanged from the zero-ROM measurement rule. LOSS: none new; the base sklearn ensembles (ExtraTrees/RF regressor, 4-class classifier, gate/router/severity experts) are kept, so any effect is attributable to hyperparameters, calibration and data dose, not to a new objective. TRAINING: CPU-only, deterministic seed 7, subject-group CV on dev, cv_folds 5, ensemble_seeds 5, blend_step 0.05, min_family_rows 12, use_metadata true, <=40 iterations per estimator; eval labels never read or used for tuning. PREDICTION: calibrated blended score; defect flags from the zero-ROM calibrated rule, thresholds optionally selected on dev out-of-fold only and reported as dev-tuned. EXPORT: preds.jsonl, calibration.json (<=1 KB), config.json including the exact DEFAULTS keys actually applied, rom_estimate.json, per-class F1 with support, and dev/dose flags under runs/<run_id>/; state explicitly that no fp16 state_dict is produced on this zero-ROM path. METRICS are computed only by the independent evaluator on the identical frozen split used by c1.

hypotheses: H1 (reference, measurable now): the zero-ROM score_moe reference, executed on release v1 with seed 7, yields a measurable PLCC/SRCC on the 85-row development_test split within the 0.66-0.85 documentation band, without any pretrained backbone; this is the first attributable measurement in this task after the iteration-1 asset outage.

H2 (gate dominates): PLCC is limited by the good-vs-defective gate rather than the severity experts, so any PLCC change should track gate accuracy/ROC-AUC, not severity-fit changes; the oracle-gate PLCC ~0.85 claim (plugin docstring) is an upper reference, not a measured result.

H3 (calibration): a monotone calibration fitted on dev out-of-fold predictions can raise PLCC by >= 0.01 but cannot change SRCC at all (rank-preserving), so any observed SRCC change must come from the hyperparameter change, not the calibration.

H4 (augmentation dose): expanding hflip coverage to 240 flipped rows (vs 0 and 120) does not lower dev PLCC by more than 0.01 but may raise supported-class macro-F1 by >= 0.01; a flare per-class F1 drop would falsify label-preservation for that class.

H5 (structural cap): the 5-class defect_macro_f1 gate 0.85 is unattainable under current label coverage (white_balance support 0 -> ceiling 0.80) and flare (3 dev_test positives < MIN_CLASS_SUPPORT 5) is unmeasurable; this is a coverage fact, not a model-quality statement.
H6 (grade agreement): grade_agreement at the configured bins (85/70/50) is measurable on this split and is more likely to clear 0.90 than PLCC/SRCC, because it only requires coarse bucket membership.

H7 (unresolvable noise): the good-class pseudo-MOS values 88.0-95.9 are derived from a filename hash, so pixel-independent variance is irreducible and any PLCC near 0.85 is at the ceiling for this benchmark, not a comfortable target.
Defect Macro-F1 is dominated by the blur, over_exp, under_exp classes; the frozen eval cannot measure white_balance (0 positives).
Weak classes carried over from feedback: none identified yet.
A frozen MobileCLIP2-S0 encoder with light multi-task heads reaches the ROM budget with headroom while beating the rule baseline on defect F1.
Class-balanced BCE + threshold tuning recovers rare-class recall without regressing the frequent classes.
controls: A0: c1 unchanged score_moe under the identical frozen split, seed 7 and evaluator metric code; sole source of delta attribution.
A1: c2 code with augmentation dose 0 -> isolates calibration + hyperparameter effect from any data effect.
A2/A3: c2 code with dose 120 and 240 -> dose-response for the materialised hflip data (requires an 'augmented' tag in the release; otherwise declared unmeasurable).
A4: identity calibration vs isotonic-on-dev-OOF -> isolates the calibration contribution and tests H3.
A5: plugin-default defect thresholds vs dev-OOF tuned thresholds -> isolates threshold tuning from model change; thresholds tuning only reported as dev-tuned.

Shared: frozen eval split and metric implementation for every variant; eval labels never used for fitting or selection; ROM estimate recorded per export; no candidate may alter labels, drop hard samples or lower floors.
Negative control for the data op: re-run A1 and A2 twice with different seeds to check the augmentation delta exceeds seed-to-seed noise before any claim.
Interface control: ast.parse plus a 5-row dry prediction before the full c2 run, because 2/2 fix attempts are already consumed.

data_recipe.description: Frozen iqa_agent benchmark: 410 labelled dev rows (train/val, subject-disjoint) + 610-image frozen eval (labels held out of the method's data dir). Label-gap classes are filled offline: local_largemodel/qwen3.8-27b proposes candidate defect labels (scripts/iqa_annotate.py, prompt iqa-prelabel-v1) and every candidate goes through human review before it can enter a dataset version; classes with no measurable support receive severity-matched augmentation (see the data plan in the research report).
data_recipe.isolation: subject-group-disjoint train/val; eval labels never exposed to the method; augmentation never touches the frozen eval in the same protocol version

operations.hypothesis: Extending hflip coverage from 120/325 to 240/325 train rows (non-overlapping subset, distinct seed) is a dose increase that reduces variance of the frozen-feature MoE heads: at dose 120 and 240 dev supported-class macro-F1 exceeds dose 0 by >= 0.01 while dev PLCC stays within +/-0.01. Counter-signal falsifying label-preservation: flare per-class F1 falls monotonically with dose, because hflip changes glare/light-source geometry. Closes the augmentation experiment that release v1 materialised but iteration 1 never trained on.
